question.text: A sophisticated HNI investor who can accept limited liquidity and seeks alternative-strategy exposure through long-short or hedge-fund style investing might prefer:

answer.text: Category III AIF using hedge-fund / long-short strategies

explanation.text: The Logic: The source workbook describes AIFs as privately pooled, non-traditional vehicles for HNIs and sophisticated investors and identifies Category III AIFs as the segment using hedge-fund / long-short type strategies with derivatives, short-selling and leverage. That profile fits an investor seeking alternative-strategy exposure and willing to accept limited liquidity. The Trap: ELSS is an equity mutual fund tax-saver, not an alternative-strategy vehicle. A savings account offers liquidity but no alternative exposure. A gold-only ETF gives commodity exposure but does not match the long-short / hedge-fund strategy ask. Note: Only the HNI / sophisticated-investor positioning of AIFs and the Category III hedge-fund / long-short characterisation are anchored to the cited pages.
